observation_summary: The Frequency.addValue(Object) method allowed non-comparable objects to be added, which caused subsequent operations to fail with ClassCastException or return incorrect results. The API contract was insufficiently restrictive.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved changing the method signature to accept 'Comparable<?>' instead of 'Object'. This is a classic interface contract mismatch where the implementation expected a specific capability (comparability) that the original signature did not enforce, leading to runtime failures. By updating the signature, the API now correctly enforces the required contract at the boundary.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'The addValue(Object v) method allows one to add a plain Object, but one cannot add anything further to the instance... it should only allow Comparable objects.'
The fix_diff_oracle shows the method signature changed from 'addValue(Object v)' to 'addValue(Comparable<?> v)'.
The stack trace shows a ClassCastException occurring because the internal TreeMap implementation requires comparable objects.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a constraint, the primary mechanism is changing the API contract (signature) to enforce the requirement at the entry point, rather than just adding a runtime guard inside an existing method.
This is a refinement of an existing API contract rather than the addition of a missing design-level capability.
